inventory_summary: Inventoried 14 sauna parts, 17 ShelfBanks, study booth bench/desk/leaf, attic built-in + bridge, nook, BED1-3 and master PAX sets, BILLY/HEMNES/SEKTION cases, millwork.md rows. Measured bbox/z vs clear faces from the resolved canvas_objects; read A-505, A-506, A-101..A-104; pdftotext of the Harvia HPCS11U1H manual. NOT examined: A-301.x/elevation sheets (no built-in interior elevations exist in the set), IKEA web listings (trusted cited rows), window stools (O4), nook SEKTION hardware, per-sheet detail of A-102/103 at 1/8in scale (too small to read dimensions).
verified_clean: BENCH booth: bench 48.875in = desk 29 + leaf 19.875, 0.8125in per end to gypsum matches walnut return 3/4in + 1/16in scribe (study_booth.md); desk 29.5in vs occupied seat 19.5in = 10in drop.
Sauna slat check: 3/4in x 3.5in basswood, P=85 lb, L=16in -> 340 in-lb, 1,037 psi, 0.040in deflection reproduced by hand (E 1.46e6, MOR 8,700).
Sauna slat layout: 7x3.5+6x0.5 = 27.5in in 28in; 5 slats in 20in; 3x3 in 10in step; bearer counts keep spans <= 16in at 78in and 58.5in.

Harvia HPCS11U1H manual (pdftotext): A 1.2in, B 4in, C 32.5in, min room 78in, 16/15/45in body, 141-636 cu ft, bench-to-ceiling max 47in; model: heater 16x15x45, 2.75in east, 3.25in south, 10.5in to reading deck, 4in to junction box, 40.8in over upper bench.
SB-A-STUDY: 1in oak, 31.25in bay, 9.875in deep, 30 lb/ft, E1.6e6 -> 0.024in vs 0.052in limit (reproduced); 3 bays + 4 partitions + 2 5/8in filler = 99.375in case.
Pantry shelves 1 1/4in oak 35.5in span 250 lb: 0.050in vs L/360 0.099in reproduced.

S4S sizes in millwork: 4/4->3/4, 5/4->1in, 6/4->1 1/4, 8/4->1 1/2, 12/4->2 1/4 (owner-milled from rough; rough width = finished + 3/4in) all achievable from owner rough stock; not a defect despite NHLA S2S 13/16, 1-1/16, 1-3/4.
Grain: walnut front horizontal along the 48.875in; desk 29x16 and leaf 19.625x16 both run E-W, matching memory (grain follows longer dimension) and the desk it butts.
IKEA catalog sizes: BILLY 31.5x11x79.5, HEMNES 35 3/8x14 5/8x77 1/2, PAX 39 3/8/19 5/8x22 7/8x92 7/8, SEKTION 90in frame on 4.5in legs = 94.5in.
Closet: north wall 32 + 39.375 + 39.375 + 0.5in scribe = 111.25in = clear 101.375..212.625; rod lines 79in/39in.
Study bridge: casing east leg 259 3/8..262 7/8, infill 262 7/8..269 3/8, built-in filler start 269 3/8 are contiguous at y=105.75.

findings.title: Sauna locust base (0.75in thick, 3.5in tall) runs behind benches that stop 0.19in off the north liner

evidence.measured: Upper bench and lower platform north faces at y=116.19in vs north clear face y=116.375in (gap 0.19in); west gap 0.75in, south reading deck 0.75in. TRIM-STANDARD gives RM-B-SAUNA a 0.75x3.5in locust base on all five wall runs (base_runs thickness_m 0.75in, height 3.5in), so a base standing proud of the liner overlaps the bench/post footprint by 0.56in on the north run and exactly touches on west/south.
evidence.expected: Bench ends scribed to the base face (>= 0.75in + 1/16in) or base omitted behind benches (RoomTrim excluding the bench runs)
evidence.method: Probe scratchpad I3/sauna.py (canvas_objects bbox vs room.clear_face) and I3/b.py (model.base_runs for RM-B-SAUNA). Sauna benches are authored from 'finished liner faces' (sauna_types.py) with no base allowance.

findings.source: TRIM-STANDARD RoomTrim for RM-B-SAUNA (millwork.py); sauna_types.py UPPER_/BENCH_NORTH_Y_IN
findings.proposed_fix: Either drop base in the sauna (benches/posts sit on the floor, base is not needed behind them in a wet hot room) or pull bench north end to 115.6in. Verify whether posts or bearers actually reach the floor at the north wall.

findings.title: REG-B-SAUNA exhaust hatch footprint is oriented 90 degrees wrong on the west liner (11in plate sticking into the room)

evidence.measured: Resolved canvas object: position (126.19, 38.0)in, rotation_degrees 0.0, footprint x 120.69..131.69 (11in) by y 37.75..38.25 (0.5in) on W-B-SA-W, a wall running along y whose clear face is x=122.5in. Every other wall register on a y-running wall has rotation +-90 and dy > dx. Centre is 5.5in (half of 11) plus -1.8125in normal_gap off the wall, i.e. the 11in width was treated as depth.
evidence.expected: Plate 0.5in deep in x, 11in wide in y, centred about x=122.5-ish (recessed), footprint dx 0.5 dy 11
evidence.method: scratchpad I3/s3.py, s4.py (canvas_objects Register with attachment_wall; compare footprint bbox)

findings.source: memory register-type-orientation; type authored (face width, depth)
findings.proposed_fix: Authored rotation_offset=-90 appears to double-rotate; try rotation_offset 0 and re-read footprint dx/dy; check the same for REG-B-SUP3 (ceiling type, fine).

findings.title: A-505/A-506 print no dimension for bench heights, headroom or heater clearance

evidence.measured: Pages 38 and 39 draw the section and wall-stack leaders only; no 42/24/12in tops, 28in depths, 40 13/16in headroom, 10.5in heater to reading deck or 4in junction-box gap are dimensioned. The 12/24/42 step sequence and Harvia clearances live only in the note.
evidence.expected: Dimensioned bench tops, widths, headroom and heater clearances (Harvia HPCS11U1H fig. 5: 1.2in side/back, 4in front, 32.5in above, 78in min room)

findings.proposed_fix: Add dimension strings to the SL-D-SAUNA slices (bench top AFF, depth, headroom) and the heater clearances

findings.title: Sauna headroom stated as 82 13/16in AFF but the model ceiling underside measures 83.06in

evidence.measured: CEIL-RM-B-SAUNA z0 = -26.375in; bench/heater base z = -109.44in; difference 83.06in. Notes and the heater source say 82 13/16in (82.81in), 40 13/16in over the upper bench and 37 13/16in above the heater; model gives 41.06in and 38.06in. A 1/4in offset (likely the floor-finish datum). Conservative direction (real headroom smaller), clears the 32.5in/78in/47in Harvia limits either way.
evidence.expected: One consistent figure between note, source string and the resolved model

findings.source: Harvia HPCS11U1H manual (fig. 5, table 2): 32.5in top, 78in room, 47in bench-to-ceiling max
findings.proposed_fix: Reconcile which datum the 82 13/16in uses and say so in the note

findings.title: PAX corner unit (93 1/8in) and adjoining PAX frames (92 7/8in) both hung 1/4in up: corner tops stand 1/4in proud

evidence.measured: Resolved top z: FURN-S-BED1-WARD 214.88in vs FURN-S-BED1-PAX-SHELF 214.63in (same mount elevation 0.25in). The product text calls the corner set '93 1/8' but its frame is 92 7/8 in the same listing; type height is 93.125 vs 92.875.
evidence.expected: Corner and frames share one top (92 7/8in + 1/4in = 93 1/8in) as the file comment says for BED3
evidence.method: scratchpad I3/fit.py (z1 of FURN-S-BED*-WARD vs PAX-SHELF)

findings.source: IKEA PAX 39 3/8 x 22 7/8 x 92 7/8in frame, listing cited in bedroom_wardrobe_types.py

findings.title: BILLY shelf stock modelled as 3/4in oak; real BILLY shelves are ~5/8in particleboard at a ~29 1/2in span

evidence.measured: ShelfBank material oak-shelf-4q, 0.75in, bay width 30in, six boards, 77in clear. Case is 31.5 x 11 x 79.5in (correct). The shelves are INCLUDED_IN_HOST so nothing is billed or milled.
evidence.expected: Bank records the bought particleboard shelf (IKEA BILLY ~16mm, inner width ~29 1/8in) or states its span/load limit
evidence.method: Inspect plan; sag of 5/8in particleboard at 29in under books exceeds L/360 at ~25 psf (computed from E~0.45e6 psi - low confidence)

findings.proposed_fix: Mark the banks as informational or correct material/thickness; add a note that heavy book loads want a mid-support or a stiffer shelf

findings.title: Plans A-101/A-102 print overlapping room labels at the sauna and study

evidence.measured: A-101 prints 'WORKSHOBAUNAL' (WORKSHOP and SAUNA labels collide); A-102 prints 'LAUNDRYSTUDY'. Built-ins in the study and sauna have no dimension strings on any plan.
evidence.expected: Legible, non-overlapping labels; built-in runs dimensioned

findings.proposed_fix: Offset the two label positions or shorten names; add built-in dimension strings in a plan or elevation

findings.title: Study nook seat top 19.5in AFF plus 3in cushion = 22.5in seat height

evidence.measured: Seat units z 121.5..141.0in (19.5in AFF), cushion 141..144 (3in thick), so loaded seat ~21-22.5in. Common seat height is 17-19in; the window-seat reading position puts knees at 22in.
evidence.expected: 17-19in loaded seat height for sustained reading, or owner-accepted

findings.proposed_fix: Owner decision; mock-up per the study-booth precedent
